Remove features associated with blank samples

mc_filter_blank.Rd

Compare feature intensities in blank and experimental groups, or remove every feature detected in a blank sample. Save the values and decisions for inspection and plotting.

mc_filter_blank(x, groups, mode = c("mean_cutoff", "drop_detected"),
    cutoff = 0.1, labels = NULL)

Arguments

x

A metabocensor_result returned by mc_prepare() or a filtering function.

groups

One or more existing group labels identifying blanks, for example "Blank". All remaining groups are treated as experimental groups in ratio mode.

mode

"mean_cutoff" (default) compares blank and experimental group means. "drop_detected" removes any feature with intensity greater than zero in any selected blank sample.

cutoff

Nonnegative blank-to-sample ratio threshold, default 0.10. Used only in "mean_cutoff" mode. A ratio equal to the cutoff does not pass.

labels

Optional sample-group labels. An unnamed vector must follow x$sample_cols; a named vector must cover those sample names exactly. NULL uses x$labels.

Details

For each feature in "mean_cutoff" mode, calculate its mean intensity within each group. Let B be the mean of the selected blank-group means, and S the largest mean among the remaining groups. Retain the feature only when B < cutoff * S. Blank groups have equal weight even if their sample counts differ.

For a positive cutoff, zero blank signal with positive sample signal passes. Positive blank signal with zero sample signal fails; zero signal in both also fails. The saved ratio is B/S, so zero denominators can produce infinite or undefined ratios. No artificial small denominator is added.

Each filtering stage can be used once per result object. To change its settings, start again from the object saved before that stage. Separate stages may be called in any order; each receives only the features retained so far.

Value

The updated result. table contains retained features, removed_ids$blank contains removed internal IDs, and counts gains a step summary. blank stores the mode and cutoff.

blank_tbl includes every feature entering this step, including removed features. Ratio mode provides Feature, Blank, Sample, Ratio, Status, and keep. Detection mode provides Feature, Detected, Status, and keep. Feature corresponds to .FID; keep is the filtering decision.

See also

mc_prepare, mc_plot_blank, mc_run

Examples

peak_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "orbi_iimn_gnps_quant.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported <- mc_prepare(
  peak_file, type = "mzmine",
  sample_keywords = c(".mzML", "Peak area")
)
metadata_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "metadata.csv",
  package = "MetaboCensoR", mustWork = TRUE
)
imported$labels <- mc_labels_from_metadata(
  metadata_file, sample_names = imported$sample_cols,
  sample_col = "Sample name", label_col = "Label"
)
after_blank <- mc_filter_blank(
  imported, groups = "Blank", mode = "mean_cutoff", cutoff = 0.10
)
head(after_blank$blank_tbl)
#>   Feature      Blank     Sample      Ratio                Status  keep
#> 1     108   161.0216   6115.185 0.02633143 Positive finite ratio  TRUE
#> 2     181  2639.1667  36148.479 0.07300907 Positive finite ratio  TRUE
#> 3     175 30666.5177 301340.100 0.10176713 Positive finite ratio FALSE
#> 4     231   391.2319  10834.849 0.03610867 Positive finite ratio  TRUE
#> 5      43   184.7637   6876.153 0.02687022 Positive finite ratio  TRUE
#> 6     145  4579.0451  50632.434 0.09043699 Positive finite ratio  TRUE
mc_summary(after_blank)
#>    step before after removed
#> 1 blank   6167  2597    3570
mc_plot_blank(after_blank, interactive = FALSE)
